course:
Tightly packed, meaningfully weighted course criteria mean the class doesn't suck each and every waking moment dry. Reading responses were very fun to do and tangibly facilitated engagement w/ course material. I'm not exactly a presentation person, but it, too was meaningfully constructed so as to be worth the time spent preparing for it. The essay assignment was my favorite, in large part due to the level of freedom granted (though all assignments provided a far greater than average level of freedom in terms of subjects).

The syllabus meaningfully pulls from a diverse array of subjects, analyzing and questioning the narratives and metanarratives around globalization and its relation to the United States. 

The readings were never too long or too much, while still being enough to allow for deep engagement for many of the subjects. I thoroughly enjoyed this course. Just due to its focal point, the 427 readings were a bit more fun.
